title: USB Colors Actually Matter!
transcript: Did you know that depending on what you're plugging into them, some USB ports may be more suitable than others? Yellow and red ports are typically always powered on unless you disconnect your system from the wall. So, that bright RGB keyboard that keeps you up at night, maybe plug that into one of your black ports. These are typically USB 2, which means they run at slower speeds that are more appropriate for peripherals like mice and keyboards. If you have a USB3 webcam, though, you're going to want to step up to a blue port. These typically run at over 10 times the speed of USB 2 and are perfect for things like capture cards and external drives. Of course, there are situations where you may want even more, and that's where teal comes in. These run at double the speed of typical USB 3 and are great for things like external SSDs or even plugging multiple devices into a single port using a hub. With all of that said, these are general guidelines and there are manufacturers who break the rules.
